chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Makhlad ibn Hamzah ibn Bayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about the earliest time of the two rak'ahs of al-Fajr, and he said: the remaining sixth of the night.

key_terms.أَوَّلِ وَقْتِ: the beginning time or earliest legal point for performing an act
key_terms.اللَّيْلِ الْبَاقِي: the remaining part of the night, meaning its final sixth
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: the two-unit prayer associated with al-Fajr

ai.seo_question: When does the time for the two rak'ahs of al-Fajr begin according to Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the earliest time for the two rak'ahs of al-Fajr. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام identifies it as the final sixth portion of the night, indicating a specific legal time related to worship.
